Title: September 3, 2026 Boulder City Council Special Meeting and Regular Meeting
Overview: The September 3, 2026 meeting covered public comment on the Frasier Meadows expansion, school closures, student rentals, and Spruce Pool funding, along with state housing laws and a set of routine items. Council approved the consent agenda, including the 2025-26 evaluations and salary adjustments for the city manager, city attorney, and municipal judge, with one dissent on that item, and approved the pedal cab licensing ordinance 7 to 0. Council also declined to call up the Frasier Meadows project because the motion failed for lack of a second, gave direction 5 to 3 to support the Boulder County commissioner expansion ballot measure, and directed informal outreach with restaurant owners and small businesses instead of forming a task force.

Topic1.Title: Special Meeting Executive Session
Topic1.Summary: Council convened a special meeting and voted unanimously to enter executive session to receive confidential legal advice regarding authorized uses of city open space. Council returned to public session after the executive session concluded at 5:17 p.m. with no concerns raised on the record.

Topic2.Title: Public Comment on Frasier Meadows Expansion and Panka Place Vacation
Topic2.Summary: Many residents spoke against the Frasier Meadows expansion, a 55-foot, 96-unit senior living project, and the proposed vacation of Panka Place. Concerns included height and setback exemptions, neighborhood transition, traffic, emergency access, flood and wildfire evacuation, and the loss of a public street. Several residents asked council to call up the planning board decision for a public hearing.

Topic3.Title: Public Comment on School Closures and Neighborhood Schools
Topic3.Summary: Residents, including a Flat Irons Elementary second grader, spoke against BVSD's proposed closure of neighborhood schools. Speakers argued the closures affect housing, traffic, climate, and walkable neighborhoods, and asked council to request a one-year delay of BVSD's vote.

Topic4.Title: Public Comment on Student Rentals, Party Houses, and Noise
Topic4.Summary: Residents described party houses and stealth dorm conversions in the Hill and Grant Place areas, citing noise, trash, and loss of affordable long-term rentals. Staff said code compliance tracks noise violations and reaches out to landlords as thresholds approach, and council members asked for follow-up data and possible out-of-the-box solutions.

Topic5.Title: Public Comment on Spruce Pool Funding and Closure
Topic5.Summary: Swimmers and residents testified about the value of Spruce Pool for safety, rehabilitation, overflow aquatics, and history, and opposed proposed funding cuts for 2027 and no funding indicated for 2028. Parks and Recreation staff acknowledged the concern, said the pool is funded for one year, and committed to meeting with supporters.

Topic6.Title: Council Recognition of Mark Wallik and Pollinator Appreciation Month
Topic6.Summary: Council Member Spear read a personal tribute and the joint declaration honoring former council member Mark Wallik's seven years of service. Council Member Shuhart read the declaration for Pollinator Appreciation Month and staff presented the new citywide bee biomonitoring initiative.

Topic7.Title: Consent Agenda and Employee Evaluations
Topic7.Summary: Council approved the consent agenda 8 to 0 with one nay on item 4E, the 2025-26 performance evaluations and salary adjustments for the city manager, city attorney, and municipal judge. Members praised the staff evaluations and raised concerns about the evaluation process and oversight.

Topic8.Title: Call-Up Check-In: Frasier Meadows Site Review and Panka Place
Topic8.Summary: Council discussed the site review amendment for the Frasier and Mountain View United Methodist properties at 350 and 355 Panka Place, including the 55-foot, 96-unit building and private drive with public access easement. Staff addressed flood, energy, and affordable housing fee questions, and a motion to call up the project failed for lack of a second.

Topic9.Title: Call-Up Check-In: Excel Energy Facility Expansion
Topic9.Summary: Council reviewed a concept plan to expand the Xcel Energy service and operations facility at 2655 North 63rd Street. Staff confirmed the project is not related to the Cosmo coal ash remediation work, and no member requested a call-up.

Topic10.Title: Public Hearing: Pedal Cab Agency and Driver Licenses
Topic10.Summary: Council held a public hearing and second reading of Ordinance 8757 creating agency and driver licenses for pedal cabs, including insurance, background checks, traffic compliance, and a ban on selling products while operating. Council approved the ordinance 7 to 0 after staff explained the licensing framework modeled on Denver and Colorado Springs.

Topic11.Title: Matters: State Legislation on Prop 123, TOC Bill, and HOME Act
Topic11.Summary: Staff briefed council on three state laws: Proposition 123 fast-track review for affordable housing, the Transit Oriented Communities bill requiring housing opportunity goals near transit, and the HOME Act for qualifying properties on underutilized land. Council gave direction to pursue removing call-ups for form-based code reviews and affordable projects, and to explore reducing ground floor retail requirements.

Topic12.Title: Restaurant and Small Business Task Force Proposal
Topic12.Summary: Council Members Tina and Matt proposed informal conversations among restaurant owners, workers, and business groups to build relationships and explore mutually beneficial solutions. Council unanimously gave direction to pursue the idea without creating an official task force or staff workload.

Topic13.Title: Council Position on Boulder County Ballot Measure to Expand Commissioners
Topic13.Summary: Council discussed whether to support the Boulder County ballot measure to change the board of county commissioners from three to five members. Members debated whether it is appropriate for the city to weigh in on another governing body's structure, with concerns about districting and representation. Council gave direction 5 to 3 to take a support position.
